items.headline: Hex.pm reports a breach of its package registry through a flaw rated at the highest severity
items.what: Hex.pm, the package registry used by Elixir and Erlang developers, said an attacker ran commands on six of its production servers on November 23 after exploiting a flaw in how the registry reads request data. The flaw carries the maximum CVSS score of 10.0. Hex.pm said it found no sign that any package was changed, but it could not rule out that the attacker read account data such as email addresses, password hashes and two-factor authentication secrets. Every account holder has been logged out and is asked to change their password and reset two-factor authentication.
items.why: Package registries sit at the center of software supply chains, so a breach there can reach every project that downloads from them. The flaw had been present in the registry code since 2016, which shows how long a weakness in trusted infrastructure can go unnoticed.
